title: C01 Auth/session foundation (FROZEN interface; attack-the-toy then real impl)

files_forbidden: all app/(challenges)/* directories not belonging to this task

acceptance_criteria: lib/auth/index.ts exports a FROZEN, documented public interface — getSession, createSession, destroySession (plus a Session type) — that downstream tasks import unchanged; the file carries a comment marking it frozen and is the only auth module other challenges may import.

Part A (attack lab) under solutions/c01-auth/insecure/ ships a deliberately naive, tamperable session (e.g. unsigned/plaintext cookie) with a README that explains exactly how to forge/tamper it; this insecure code lives ONLY under solutions/ and is never imported by the live app (QA: reference solutions stored separately from starters).

Part B under solutions/c01-auth/secure/ implements the real session on a vetted library (jose or iron-session) with a signed/encrypted token; a forged or tampered cookie is rejected (signature/decrypt failure) and treated as no session (QA: a forged or tampered session cookie is rejected).

login route establishes a session via createSession and logout route clears it via destroySession; after logout getSession returns null, and the session secret is read from a server-only source never shipped to the client (QA: server-only secret isolation — no secret in client bundle).

The c01 _meta folder contains spec.md, defend-it.md (3-5 from-memory questions WITH model answers), verification.md, and a challenge.config.ts that the registry can discover; defend-it.md is committed and non-empty (QA: every challenge has a committed Defend-It artifact).
output_format: code plus plain English explanation of every non-obvious decision
